data.one_liner: Approval tests implementation in Dart for snapshot and complex object testing.
data.what_it_does: Approval tests provide an alternative to traditional assertions by taking a snapshot of test results (such as long strings, collections, or JSON objects) and comparing them against a saved approved file. If a mismatch occurs, reporters highlight the differences.
use_when: Testing objects with complex values, long strings, or many properties
Verifying complex JSON model outputs against a baseline snapshot
Running unit tests where exact string or text output comparison is required
avoid_when: Testing simple primitive equality where standard expect(actual, equals(expected)) is sufficient
Projects requiring heavy visual/UI golden testing specifically for Flutter widgets (use approval_tests_flutter instead)
strengths: Simplifies assertions for large or complex structured outputs
Supports automatic file generation and CLI-based review workflows
Includes atomic text writing and strict mode options for CI environments
weaknesses: Requires maintaining approved baseline files alongside source or test code
Depends on correct file naming and path resolution conventions
data.setup_notes: Add approval_tests to dev_dependencies/dependencies in pubspec.yaml and configure test files.

alternatives.name: test
alternatives.why_pick_it: For basic standard unit testing assertions without file-based snapshots.
